text:
mira: Heads-up — embedding route 'embeddings.generate' is seeing KV cache saturation on emb-primary. P99 token latency jumped from ~120ms to ~2.4s for last 10m, error rate creeping up for some customers. Alert fired: kv-saturation-high.

oncall-bot: ALERT: kv-saturation-high (prod) — routed to team-sre. Pager: sent to @dan (primary) and @kevin (secondary).

mira: quick context — traffic spike from a large customer + a prefetch bug combined. Eviction rate up ~5x, cache hit drops to ~62%. Queue depth on emb-primary worker pool ~1200.

dan: I see it in metrics. Logs show frequent cache misses and lookups blocked on disk: "ERROR kv_backend: io timeout". Moving to mitigation steps now.

kevin: I can take secondary responsibilities if we shift traffic. Current primary/secondary: primary=dan, secondary=kevin. Dan, hand me the pass if you want me to adjust route weights.

mira: Runbook refs: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kv-saturation (pager play), and quick mitigation checklist in the runbook -> section 'fast fallbacks'.

jamie: Quick checklist I'm running through:
- disable prefetch for embeddings (it floods backfills)
- scale emb-primary read replicas up by 1-2 nodes
- enable read-only fallback for low-priority customers
- shift 30% traffic to embeddings-secondary
dan: Doing commands now:
```
# scale primary pool
kubectl -n prod scale sts emb-primary-workers --replicas=6
# disable prefetch flag
redwoodctl feature-flag set embeddings_prefetch false --env=prod
```

oncall-bot: NOTE: change detected in feature flags: embeddings_prefetch toggled to false by dan.

dan: Scaling completed. Watching p99 — small improvement after scale: 2.4s -> 1.9s. Still high. Evictions trending down but hit-rate still poor.

kevin: I'm taking the route change. Applying weighted routing to move 35% to secondary for a quick protective shift.

jamie: Route change applied via control plane: emb-route weights now primary=65, secondary=35. Monitoring customer impact — will hold for 10m.

mira: Customer impact: two mid-sized customers (acct IDs acct-321, acct-888) reported slow responses and a few retries. No full outage. SRE escalation in place; CS notified to stand by for comms if needed.

dan: Also queued a rolling restart of a subset of emb-primary pods to clear stuck workers (1/3 batches). Command:
```
kubectl -n prod rollout restart sts/emb-primary-workers --max-unavailable=1
```

sre-bot: Action logged — restart staged. Expected brief connection churn for restarted pods.

kevin: After the weight shift and restart, p99 now ~720ms, p95 ~210ms, hit-rate ~84%. Error counts reduced by ~40%. Good signs but stay in watch.

mira: Handoff notes for next on-call window (primary change incoming at 02:00 UTC):
- primary: kevin (takes over at 02:00 UTC), secondary: jamie
- current mitigations in effect: embeddings_prefetch=false, route weights primary=65/secondary=35, emb-primary scaled to 6, rolling restarts ongoing
- active alerts: kv-saturation-high (watch), emb-ingress-queue-depth (informational)
- outstanding tasks: follow full eviction-latency root cause (likely mutation pattern from acct-321), confirm disk/io ops healthy on affected nodes, run deeper tracing for cold-key hotspots
- contacts: dan (current primary), kevin (incoming primary), mira (incident lead), SRE pager group
- runbook pointers: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kv-saturation and https://redwood.internal/playbooks/route-weighting
dan: Any coverage gaps? We don't have an infra person on call until 03:00 UTC — if disk IO deteriorates we'll need an infra on-call to patch kernel/nvme settings. Marking as potential escalation.

mira: Noted — escalation path: infra-oncall -> page via pagerduty tag infra-prod. If p99 > 2s again or error rate spikes 3x, escalate.

kevin: I'll take over at 02:00 UTC. Plan on keeping current mitigations 30-60m then start a staged rollback of route weights if stable. I'll also follow up with CS about acct-321 protection.

mira: Thanks — leaving this thread for the pass. Attach logs + short clips in the incident channel if anything changes. :thumbsup:
